label: Pruss power premises: laws, nonvacuity, collective/distributive separations, omissions, rivals
paraphrase: Premise-free laws and finite models (structural surrogates, not metaphysical possibility). Laws: (1) a one-way (fixed) giver existing at w has no power for the actual contingents' joint absence satisfying P2-delta; (2) P1-prime, P2-delta, P4-prime and P5 exclude that every being at w is a fixed giver; (3) collapse: a fixed giver necessary at w, with factive giving, gives being at w only to beings necessary at w; (4) necessary fixed-output (deterministic) sources: if every concrete being contingent at w is given being at w by some necessary fixed giver (one or an aggregate), with factive giving, none is contingent (a chancy necessary source is not a fixed giver and is not covered); (5) under the holders-give-each reading with factive giving, P2-prime and P5 give P2-delta; (6) the joint absence realized by withholding, with P5, gives a two-way giver that is not a fixed giver; (7) Pruss's direction relocates the abstention: a being at w and at a world lacking the actual contingents that gives one of them being at w is, with factive giving, a two-way giver; (8) a concrete being at w present, for each actual contingent concretum, at an accessible world lacking it is, with excluded middle, necessary (the joint one carries the argument); (9) with excluded middle, a holder with POWER_OVER_ESSE_1 over each actual contingent concretum makes every concrete foundational being at w necessary, without a Euclidean premise. Models: theist nonvacuity of every argument; collective without distributive (replacement on the thin reading of PowerFor: the holder has POWER_OVER_ESSE_1 over the replacement it gives being, none over the actual contingent, and the transfer fails; one actual contingent, so collective and distributive coincide here; the separation shown is PowerFor to POWER_OVER_ESSE_1, already for one member); distributive without collective (Van Cleve with a common holder: P4-prime and initiator presence fail); mutual annihilators (distributive grounding with varying holders, no necessary being); eight omission models; three rivals (inert necessary being, with P1-prime failing by the model's choice of no powers; necessary fixed-output (deterministic) source; positive-outcome powers only, under which P1-prime fails and Pruss's direction holds).
